mainTopic: When the כותים can be trusted about burial, בכור, graves and other matters they are careless about
overview: This amud finishes this פרק's discussion of the כותים and closes the פרק of דם הנדה. First the גמרא explains why the כותים don't bury נפלים: they read 'לא תסיג גבול' as teaching that only someone with a נחלה gets a burial plot. Then it asks how we can trust the כותים at all, since they don't accept לפני עור. The answer is that we rely on their own actions: a כותי כהן eating pure תרומה on the spot, or a כותי shearing and working an animal that would be forbidden if it were a בכור. Each time the גמרא adds that the כותים are knowledgeable enough to be right. They are also trusted about grave-markings, because that practice is written in a פסוק. They are not trusted about doubtful places like סככות, פרעות and a בית הפרס, unless the כותי walked over the whole area himself. The משנה's rule 'זה הכלל' adds that they are not believed about תחומין or יין נסך, and the פרק of דם הנדה closes with הדרן.

steps.title: Which verse did the כותים expound?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what פסוק the כותים used to decide that a נפל does not need burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What did they expound?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by asking what source the כותים relied on for their practice with נפלים. This is a setup question; the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה reported a practice of the כותים without giving a reason. The גמרא assumes the כותים had a reason from the תורה and wants to know which פסוק it was.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
What?
They expounded (drew a rule out of a פסוק)

phrases.english: GEMARA: What did they expound?
phrases.notes: 'They' means the כותים from the משנה, who don't bury נפלים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's statement about the כותים and נפלים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק led the כותים to conclude that a נפל needs no burial.

steps.title: The boundary verse: no inheritance means no burial plot
steps.stepSummary: The כותים expounded 'לא תסיג גבול רעך': whoever has a נחלה has a גבול (a burial place), and whoever has no נחלה has no גבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse: 'You shall not move your fellow's boundary, which the earlier ones set, in your inheritance.' Whoever has an inheritance has a boundary; whoever has no inheritance has no boundary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer: the כותים learned from the פסוק about boundaries that only someone who inherits land gets a burial place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כותים connected 'boundary' (גבול) with 'inheritance' (נחלה) in the same פסוק. They read גבול as a burial plot, so a נפל, who never inherits anything, gets no burial plot.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not move a boundary marker
Inheritance (a share in the land)
Boundary; here read as a burial place
A stillborn baby

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the כותים did not bury נפלים, which matters for whether their graveyards carry טומאה.

phrases.english: "You shall not move your fellow's boundary
phrases.notes: דברים 19:14

phrases.english: which the earlier ones set, in your inheritance."
Anyone who has an inheritance
has a boundary,
phrases.notes: Here 'boundary' means a burial plot.

phrases.english: anyone who has no inheritance
has no boundary.
phrases.notes: A נפל never inherits land, so by their reading it gets no burial plot.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא תַסִּיג גְּבוּל רֵעֲךָ אֲשֶׁר גָּבְלוּ רִאשֹׁנִים בְּנַחֲלָתְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כותים linked גבול to נחלה: only one who inherits gets a burial plot, so a נפל is not buried.

steps.title: How can we trust the כותים if they ignore לפני עור?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the כותים are believed to say 'we buried' there. The גמרא objects: they do not accept the rule of לפני עור, so they might mislead us.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They are believed to say: we buried.' But they do not hold of 'Do not put a stumbling block before the blind'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and challenges it: why trust the כותים about where נפלים are buried?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our חכמים learn from לפני עור that you may not cause someone else to sin. The כותים do not accept this, so they would not care if their testimony led a Jew into טומאה. That makes their word seem unreliable.

keyTerms.meaning: They are believed (trusted as witnesses)
They do not hold of / do not accept
The rule against causing another person to stumble or sin
A stumbling block

steps.confusionAlert: The כותים do keep many מצוות. The problem here is only that they don't accept the חכמים' reading of לפני עור, so they aren't careful about leading others into sin.

phrases.english: They are believed to say: "We buried."
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: the כותים are believed about whether they buried נפלים in a spot.

phrases.english: But they do not hold of
"And before the blind do not put a stumbling block"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:14

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה, about trusting the כותים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the כותים are believed to say 'we buried' or 'we did not bury'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone who does not accept לפני עור has no reason to avoid misleading others, so his testimony should not be relied on.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: a כותי כהן is standing on the spot
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that the משנה means a case where a כותי כהן is standing on that very spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: It is where a כהן is standing there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו limits the משנה to a case where a כותי כהן is standing on the place in question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We are not trusting their words alone. A כהן avoids טומאת מת himself, so if he stands there, it shows he truly believes the spot is not impure.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest, who must avoid טומאת מת
Standing there
The impurity that comes from a dead body

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
It is where a priest is standing there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ בְּכֹהֵן עוֹמֵד שָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה trusts the כותים' words even though they ignore לפני עור.
steps.terutzMaskana: We rely on the כהן's own behavior, which shows he really believes the spot is pure.

steps.title: Maybe the כהן is already impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: perhaps the כהן is already impure, so standing there proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he is an impure כהן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבהו's answer: a כהן who is already טמא would not care about standing on an impure spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from the כהן only works if he has something to lose. If he is already impure, his standing there tells us nothing about the spot.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
Ritually impure
A priest who is already impure

phrases.english: But perhaps he is an impure priest?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's proof from the כהן standing there.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An already impure כהן has no reason to avoid the spot, so his presence proves nothing.

steps.title: He is holding תרומה in his hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is where the כהן is holding תרומה, which shows he is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he is holding תרומה in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the case more specific: the כהן is holding תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding תרומה shows the כהן is careful about purity and considers himself pure. So he would not stand on a spot he thought was impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Holding
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן, which must stay pure
In his hand

phrases.english: Where he is holding teruma in his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן might already be impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: He holds תרומה, showing he is pure and careful.

steps.title: Maybe the תרומה itself is impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects again: perhaps the תרומה he holds is impure, so holding it proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is impure תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer: maybe the תרומה is already impure, so the כהן doesn't need to guard it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תרומה is already impure, holding it does not show that the כהן is protecting his purity. The proof falls apart again.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure תרומה

phrases.english: But perhaps it is impure teruma?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from the כהן holding תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Impure תרומה needs no protection, so holding it shows nothing about the כהן's purity or the spot.

steps.title: He is eating the תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the כהן is eating the תרומה, which shows it is pure, since impure תרומה may not be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he is eating from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final, most specific picture: the כהן is actually eating the תרומה on that spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure תרומה may not be eaten, so if he eats it, it must be pure, and he must be pure too. A pure כהן eating pure תרומה on that spot clearly believes no נפל is buried there, so the כותים can be trusted in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: He is eating
From it
Eating תרומה, allowed only when it is pure

steps.whatToRemember: The כותים are not trusted on their word alone, because they don't accept לפני עור. They are believed only when their own actions prove it: a כותי כהן eating תרומה on that spot.

phrases.english: Where he is eating from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7, giving the final picture of the case, which step 9 then questions as too obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: He eats it, and impure תרומה may not be eaten, so both he and the תרומה are pure and the spot is truly clean.

steps.title: If the case is that obvious, why teach it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the כותי כהן is eating תרומה on that spot, it is obvious he trusts it is pure, so why does the משנה need to say so?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the answer it reached in Step 8. If the case is that clear, the משנה's teaching seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 made the case so strong (a כהן eating pure תרומה right on that spot) that the ruling now looks obvious. The גמרא asks what new point the משנה is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is really the case
What is there to say? It is obvious, so why teach it?

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say?
phrases.notes: In other words: if the כהן is eating תרומה right there, of course the spot is pure. Why spell it out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case set up in Step 8 as too obvious to need teaching
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the משנה's ruling once the case is defined as a כהן eating תרומה there
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling that follows obviously from the facts has no point being taught

steps.title: We might have thought they don't know how a fetus forms
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is still needed: we might have thought the כותים cannot tell when a fetus is formed enough to make a place impure. The משנה teaches that they do know.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that they are not knowledgeable about the formation of a fetus. So the משנה teaches us that they are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 9 by showing a real doubt the משנה is removing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כותי's behavior proves he believes the spot is pure. But maybe he is simply wrong about the facts, for example thinking a fetus was too unformed to make anything impure. The משנה teaches that they understand these stages, so their behavior can be relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said... (introduces a mistaken assumption)
So it teaches us (the point the ruling adds)
Experts; knowledgeable
Formation: the stage at which a fetus is formed enough to make things impure

steps.confusionAlert: The doubt is not whether the כותי is honest. Step 8 already showed he truly believes the spot is pure. The question is whether he knows enough to be right.

phrases.english: You might have said:
they are not knowledgeable about formation,
phrases.notes: He means the stages of a fetus's growth, and when it's developed enough to make a place impure.

phrases.english: so it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9 by pointing to a real doubt the משנה removes
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the ruling teaches something new (חידוש)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כותים might honestly be mistaken about whether a fetus was formed
steps.terutzMaskana: They are knowledgeable about formation, so their behavior is reliable
steps.whatToRemember: Trusting the כותים requires two things: they must truly believe what they show (Steps 4-8), and they must know enough to be right (Step 10).

steps.title: How can we trust them about a firstborn animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next ruling in the משנה, that כותים are believed about an animal's firstborn status. It asks: the כותים don't accept the rule of לפני עור, so they might mislead us without caring.
steps.simpleTranslation: "They are believed about an animal," etc. But they don't hold of "Before the blind do not put a stumbling block"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new clause in the משנה and immediately challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כותים are believed when they say an animal already gave birth, so its next offspring is not a בכור. But the כותים don't accept the חכמים' reading of לפני עור, that one may not cause another person to sin. So they might tell a Jew the animal is not a בכור without any concern that they are leading him to sin.

keyTerms.meaning: They are believed; their testimony is trusted
Firstborn male animal, which is holy and may not be used for ordinary work
Do not put a stumbling block before the blind, read by the Sages as a ban on causing others to sin

phrases.english: They are believed about the animal, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: a כותי is believed that an animal already gave birth, so its next offspring is not a בכור.

phrases.english: But they do not hold of
"And before the blind do not put a stumbling block"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:14

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the משנה and challenges it
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that כותים are believed about an animal's firstborn status
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: People who don't care about causing others to sin cannot be trusted when their words could lead a Jew into sin

steps.title: The כותי himself is shearing and working the offspring
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the case is one where the כותי himself shears and works the offspring. Since one may not shear or work a בכור, his own behavior shows it is not a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the case is where he shears it and works with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers Step 11 by narrowing the case to one where the כותי's own actions show what he believes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We don't rely on what the כותי tells others. We rely on what he does himself. The כותים are careful about Torah law, and the Torah forbids shearing or working a בכור. So if he shears and works the animal, he clearly believes it is not a בכור. This is the same method as the כהן eating תרומה in Steps 4-8.

keyTerms.meaning: Shears (wool)
Works with the animal, using it for labor

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
When he shears and works it.
phrases.notes: "He" is the כותי himself, and "it" is the offspring. The Torah forbids shearing or working a בכור.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּגוֹזֵז וְעוֹבֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11 by narrowing the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling trusts the כותי's words to others
steps.terutzMaskana: We rely on his own behavior, which shows he truly believes it is not a בכור

steps.title: Again: if so, why teach it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question as before: if the כותי himself is shearing and working the animal, it is obvious he believes it isn't a בכור, so why does the משנה need to teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: Using the same wording as Step 9, the גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's case as too obvious to need teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the כותי's own actions prove what he believes, the ruling seems to add nothing. The גמרא looks for the new point, just as it did with the כהן eating תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Shearing and working a firstborn, which the Torah forbids. That is why his actions prove what he believes

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 12's case as too obvious
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the ruling once the כותי is shearing and working the animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If his own conduct proves his belief, the ruling seems obvious

steps.title: We might have thought they don't recognize a murky discharge
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is still needed: we might have thought the כותים cannot tell whether a murky discharge from the womb counts as a birth that cancels בכור status. The משנה teaches that they do know.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that they are not knowledgeable about a murky discharge. So the משנה teaches us that they are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 13 the same way it answered Step 9, by naming a real doubt about the כותים' knowledge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A murky discharge from an animal's womb can count as a first birth, so the next offspring is not a בכור. A כותי might honestly but wrongly think such a discharge happened. The משנה teaches that the כותים are knowledgeable in this area, so their behavior can be trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: A murky discharge from the womb, which can count as a birth and exempt later offspring from בכור status

phrases.english: You might have said:
they are not knowledgeable about a murky discharge,
phrases.notes: If the animal let out such a discharge before, that counts as giving birth, so the next one isn't a בכור. He might wrongly think it happened.

phrases.english: so it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13, matching the pattern of Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the ruling teaches something new (חידוש)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כותים might be mistaken about whether a murky discharge took place
steps.terutzMaskana: They are knowledgeable about this, so their behavior is reliable
steps.whatToRemember: Same two-part pattern as the תרומה case: the action proves sincere belief, and the משנה adds that the כותים have the needed knowledge.

steps.title: Trusted on grave-markings because it appears in a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The כותים are believed about grave-markings. Even though marking graves is only מדרבנן, the practice is written in a פסוק, so the כותים are careful about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: "They are believed about grave-markings," etc. Even though it is only rabbinic, since it is written, they are careful about it, as it says: "And he sees a human bone and builds a marker beside it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה and explains why we trust the כותים here, even though they usually ignore rabbinic laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כותים generally keep only what is written in the Torah, so we would expect them to ignore a rabbinic rule like marking graves. But since this practice is mentioned in a פסוק (in יחזקאל), they treat it seriously. So their markings are reliable, and an unmarked area can be treated as pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A marker placed over a grave to warn people of impurity
By rabbinic law, not directly from the Torah
They are very careful about it
A human bone, which makes things impure

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק is from יחזקאל, not the Torah, so marking graves is still a rabbinic law. The point is only that because it is written, the כותים respect it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the general rule for the כותים: they are trusted on whatever they are careful about, and a practice that appears in a written פסוק counts even if it is technically rabbinic.

phrases.english: They are believed about grave-marking, etc.
And even though it is rabbinic,
since it is written —
they are very careful about it,
as it is written:
"And he sees a human bone
and builds a marker beside it."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 39:15

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּמִדְּרַבָּנַן הוּא, כֵּיוָן דִּכְתִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה and explains it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כותים are trusted about grave-markings because, although the practice is rabbinic, it is written in a פסוק and they are careful about it
steps.whatToRemember: The כותים are trusted wherever they are careful, and they are careful about anything written in a פסוק, even a rabbinic practice like marking graves.

steps.title: Defining overhanging boughs and protruding stones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list of places where the כותים are not believed, and defines סככות and פרעות using other sources.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says the כותים are not believed about overhanging boughs and the like. 'Overhanging boughs' means a tree spreading over the ground. 'Protrusions' means stones sticking out of a fence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and explains what two unclear words mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are places that can form a covering over a grave or a corpse, so they can carry טומאה. The גמרא does not argue here. It only defines the words by citing other teachings so we know what the משנה is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: Overhanging boughs: tree branches that spread out over the ground
Protrusions: stones that stick out from a wall or fence
A tree that spreads over and covers the ground
A fence or stone wall

phrases.english: But they are not believed
not about overhanging boughs, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה lists places where we are unsure whether a grave or corpse is underneath, and there the כותים are not trusted.

phrases.english: Overhanging boughs: as we learned:
"These are overhanging boughs:
a tree that spreads over the ground."
Protrusions: as we learned:
"Protruding stones that stick out of a fence."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אֵין נֶאֱמָנִין לֹא עַל הַסְּכָכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case where the כותים are believed (grave-markings) to the cases where they are not.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סככות are trees spreading over the ground; פרעות are stones jutting out of a fence.

steps.title: You may blow on a בית הפרס and walk through
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל teaches that a person may blow the dirt of a בית הפרס in front of him as he walks through it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה mentions a בית הפרס. רב יהודה said in the name of רב שמואל: a person may blow on a בית הפרס and keep walking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next term in the משנה, בית הפרס, and gives a practical rule for walking through one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית הפרס is a field where a grave was plowed up, so small bones may be scattered in it. By blowing the dust away, a person can uncover any bone and avoid touching it. Then he can cross while staying טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: A field where a grave was plowed up, so it may have scattered bones
Blows (on the dirt)
And walks on

phrases.english: A beit haperas.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav Shmuel said:
A person may blow on a beit haperas
phrases.notes: Blowing moves the dust, so a hidden bone gets uncovered and he can step around it.

phrases.english: and walk on.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית הַפְּרָס. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the משנה's list by moving to בית הפרס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may blow the dirt in front of him in a בית הפרס and walk through.

steps.title: A trampled בית הפרס is pure
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר אמי, in the name of רב יהודה, teaches that a בית הפרס that has been trodden down by people is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר אמי said in the name of רב יהודה: a בית הפרס that has been trampled is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another rule about a בית הפרס: once many people have walked on it, it is treated as טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry in a בית הפרס is small bone pieces lying on the ground. When many people trample it, we assume those bones were crushed or carried away. So the worry is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: That was trodden or trampled down
Pure (not carrying טומאה)

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Ami said in the name of Rav Yehuda:
A beit haperas that has been trodden is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rule about בית הפרס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית הפרס that has been trampled by people is טהור.

steps.title: How large an area becomes a בית הפרס
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that plowing a graveyard makes a בית הפרס, and sets its size. רבי יוסי gives a larger size.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: someone who plows a graveyard makes it a בית הפרס. How far does it reach? A full furrow of 100 אמות, an area for sowing four סאין. רבי יוסי says: five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains how a בית הפרס is made and how much land it covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plowing can drag bones out of a grave and spread them across the field. The תנא קמא says this spread covers a full furrow of 100 by 100 אמות, an area that takes four סאין of seed. רבי יוסי says the area is bigger: five סאין.

keyTerms.meaning: One who plows
A graveyard
A full furrow: the length a plow goes before turning
An area that takes four סאין of seed to sow

steps.whatToRemember: A בית הפרס is made by plowing a grave. Its worry is scattered bones. Blowing on the dirt lets a person walk through while staying pure, and heavy trampling makes the field pure. Plowing spreads this status over an area of 100 by 100 אמות (רבי יוסי: a little more).

phrases.english: And it was taught: One who plows a graveyard
makes it a beit haperas.
And how far does he make it?
A full furrow, one hundred cubits,
phrases.notes: This means a square area, 100 אמות by 100 אמות.

phrases.english: an area for sowing four se'a.
Rabbi Yosei says: Five.
phrases.notes: He means five סאין of seed, a slightly larger area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the topic with a ברייתא defining how a בית הפרס is made and how big it is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plowing a graveyard makes a בית הפרס of a full furrow (100 אמות, four סאין of seed). רבי יוסי says five.

steps.title: But a ברייתא trusts a כותי about a lost grave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: a ברייתא says a כותי is believed to say there is no grave in a field where a grave was lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they really not believed? But it was taught: about a field in which a grave was lost, a כותי is believed to say, 'There is no grave there.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule that the כותים are not believed about a בית הפרס, using a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A field where a grave was lost has the same status as a בית הפרס. The משנה says a כותי is not believed there, but the ברייתא says he is. The גמרא is setting up a contradiction, which רבי יוחנן resolves in Step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: They are believed (trusted as witnesses)
A field in which a grave was lost (its exact spot is unknown)
There is no grave there

phrases.english: And are they not believed?
But wasn't it taught: A field in which a grave was lost,
phrases.notes: This kind of field counts as a בית הפרס, just like the one in the משנה.

phrases.english: a Samaritan is believed to say
"There is no grave there."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה's rule about בית הפרס that the previous steps were explaining.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that כותים are not believed about a בית הפרס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says a כותי is believed about a field where a grave was lost, which is a kind of בית הפרס. This contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: The ברייתא's reason, and the overhanging tree
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא used in the challenge explains why the כותי is believed: he is testifying about the grave itself. It adds the same rule for a tree hanging over the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is believed because he is only testifying about the grave itself. The same goes for a tree that hangs over the ground: he is believed to say there is no grave under it, because he is only testifying about the grave itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא that challenges our משנה. The ברייתא gives its reason, and then adds the case of an overhanging tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the כותי is not judging a doubtful case. He is saying the grave itself is not there, and that is a Torah matter, which כותים are careful about. The tree case makes the challenge sharper, because our משנה said כותים are NOT believed about overhanging branches (סככות).

keyTerms.meaning: The grave itself, meaning the actual presence of a real grave
A tree
Hangs over or covers, like branches spreading over the ground
Because

steps.confusionAlert: This is still the challenge from Step 20, not a new ruling. The tree case is exactly the kind of סככות the משנה said a כותי is NOT believed about. That is why it is a problem.

phrases.english: because he is not testifying
phrases.notes: This finishes the ברייתא from Step 20, about a field where a grave was lost.

phrases.english: except about the grave itself.
A tree that hangs over the ground —
he is believed to say, "There is no grave under it,"
because he is not testifying
except about the grave itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵעִיד אֶלָּא עַל גּוּפוֹ שֶׁל קֶבֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא that Step 20 brought as a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that כותים are not believed about סככות and בית הפרס-type cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא believes a כותי about a lost grave and an overhanging tree. The משנה does not believe him about such places.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the כותי walked over the whole area
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the ברייתא is talking about a כותי who walked back and forth over the entire area.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It is talking about a case where he walks back and forth over all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge. He says the ברייתא is about a כותי who walked over every part of the area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כותי walked over the whole area himself, he would have become טמא if a grave were there. So his word shows he really believes there is no grave. In the משנה's case he did not walk over it all, so we do not trust him, because כותים are not careful in doubtful cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Walks back and forth
Over the whole of it, meaning the entire area

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common way the גמרא solves a contradiction: each source is talking about a different case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is where he walks back and forth over all of it.
phrases.notes: "All of it" means the whole field, or the whole area under the tree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בִּמְהַלֵּךְ וּבָא עַל פְּנֵי כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases: the ברייתא is about a כותי who walked over the whole area
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא trusts a כותי about overhanging places in general, against the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is only trusted when he walked over the whole area himself. Otherwise the משנה's rule stands.

steps.title: If so, why say it at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if he walked over the whole area, it is obvious he is believed. Why does the ברייתא need to teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is it telling us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's answer. If the כותי walked everywhere, of course he is believed, so the ברייתא seems pointless. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רבי יוחנן limits the ברייתא to such a clear case, the ruling looks too obvious to teach. The גמרא expects every teaching to tell us something we would not have known.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why say it? Meaning it seems obvious

phrases.english: If so, what is the point of saying it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's answer by saying it makes the ברייתא too obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching that only says something obvious would be pointless.

steps.title: We might have worried about a narrow strip
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is still needed. We might have thought a narrow strip of the field reaches elsewhere and the grave is there, so the ברייתא teaches us not to worry about that.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that a strip of the field reaches out somewhere else. So it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of why the ברייתא is needed. Without it, we might have doubted even a כותי who walked over the whole field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe a narrow strip with the same field name reaches into another area, and the כותי thinks the grave is there. Then his walking over the main part proves nothing, and he would be treating it as only a doubt. The ברייתא teaches that we do not worry about this, so he is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said, the start of a mistaken first thought
A strip, a narrow band of land
Goes out, reaches out
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: A כותי is believed that there is no grave only if he walked over the whole area himself. We do not worry that the grave is in some far-off strip of the field.

phrases.english: You might have said: a strip goes out,
phrases.notes: He means a narrow strip of the same field that reaches somewhere else, where the כותי might think the grave is.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: רְצוּעָה נָפְקָא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the ברייתא is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a worry the ברייתא removes, so the teaching is not obvious
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even after walking over the field, the כותי might think the grave is in a strip somewhere else, so he should not be believed.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not worry about such a strip, so the כותי who walked over the whole field is believed.

steps.title: What does 'this is the rule' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'זה הכלל' and asks what extra cases they come to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: "This is the rule..." What does "this is the rule" come to add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה, 'זה הכלל', and asks what it includes. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule is that in any matter כותים are suspected about, they are not believed. The גמרא assumes a general rule like this teaches about cases not already listed, so it asks which ones.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the rule, a general rule in a משנה
What does it come to include?

phrases.english: "This is the rule," etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה: in any matter they are suspected about, they are not believed.

phrases.english: "This is the rule" comes to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the grave discussion and turns to the משנה's general rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which extra cases the משנה's general rule includes.

steps.title: It includes תחומין and יין נסך
steps.stepSummary: 'זה הכלל' adds that כותים are not believed about תחומין (שבת walking limits) or about יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include שבת boundaries and wine poured for idols.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule adds two areas where a כותי's word is not accepted: תחומין and יין נסך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תחומין are a rabbinic rule, and כותים are not careful about it, so they cannot tell us where a תחום ends. They also do not keep away from wine a non-Jew touched, so they are not believed that wine is not יין נסך.

keyTerms.meaning: שבת boundaries, the limit of how far one may walk on שבת
Wine poured for idols, or wine forbidden because of that

steps.whatToRemember: The rule: a כותי is not believed about anything he himself is not careful about. This includes תחומין and יין נסך.

phrases.english: To include Shabbos boundaries and wine poured for idols.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what 'זה הכלל' adds.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It adds that כותים are not believed about תחומין or יין נסך.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the perek of דם הנדה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the פרק called דם הנדה with the traditional הדרן line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, 'דם הנדה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The learning of this פרק is finished, and the text says the traditional goodbye line, הדרן, to mark the end of the chapter. This is not an argument or a new law. It is a closing statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of the last steps ended with the answer about 'זה הכלל', which said כותים are not believed about תחומין or יין נסך. Now the פרק is officially closed. The words 'דם הנדה' are the chapter's name, taken from the opening words of its first משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you': the traditional line said when finishing a פרק
The name of this פרק, taken from its first words
A chapter of a מסכת

steps.whatToRemember: The פרק of דם הנדה ends here. Its last discussion was about when a כותי is believed, and the rule of 'זה הכלל' that they are not believed about תחומין or יין נסך.
steps.confusionAlert: 'דם הנדה' here is not a new law about blood. It is just the name of the chapter being closed.

phrases.english: We will return to you,
phrases.notes: This is the line said when finishing a chapter, a promise to come back and learn it again.

phrases.english: 'The blood of a נדה.'
phrases.notes: This is the name of the chapter, taken from its first words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the פרק after the final answer about 'זה הכלל' in step 26.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The seventh פרק of מסכת נדה, דם הנדה, is complete.
